banks.name: Federal Reserve

sources.label: FXEmpire (Oct 19): Fed hike bets fade — Oct hold ~84%, Dec hike ~92%
finanzen.ch (Oct 19): Warsh won't prejudge October; wait until December
DailyForex (Oct 19): Forex today — Oct FOMC hold ~84-87%
ActionForex: Fed hike odds Oct 20 — ~17% Oct hike prob (hold ~83%)

banks.detail: October priced as a hold at ~83-85% (CME FedWatch ~83%; ActionForex/Kalshi) into the Oct 17-29 blackout. Warsh gave no October signal at the IMF meetings — December is the debate, but the range is wide (~70% Jin10 Oct 12 vs ~92% FXEmpire Oct 19). 10Y 5.14% (+7-9bp Monday); 2Y 4.77%. Hot week stands: import prices +1.1% (+8.1% y/y, 4-yr high); TIC Aug +$199.8B (foreign bid intact).
banks.summary: The Fed is expected to hold in October, then decide on a hike in December. Recent inflation has run hot, which keeps the dollar supported while markets wait.

banks.name: Bank of Canada
banks.priced: October 28: hike now the base case (~83-87% OIS); December: further hike ~68%.

sources.label: Wealth Professional (Oct 13): October BoC hike odds down to 25%
TD via Mitrade (Oct 17): Canada CPI forecast 3.2% y/y
ActionForex (Oct 20): BoC Oct-28 hike odds jump to 82.8% on Macklem remarks

banks.detail: MASSIVE repricing Monday: Oct-28 hike odds jumped from ~1-in-4 (Oct 18) to 82.8-87% (OIS, ActionForex/BlueGamma) after Macklem's Saturday remarks that the BoC will revise its inflation forecast substantially higher on energy. CONFLICT: Reuters' Oct 19 CPI piece still cites money markets betting on a hold (bankofcanadaodds.com: 78% hold) — two measures disagree; OIS is the fresher read. Dec 9: ~68% further hike; ~104bp cumulative priced by Sep 2027. Data argues hold: Sep CPI mild miss (3.1% vs 3.2%), jobs -68.3K, unemployment 6.5% — but the market now believes Macklem.
banks.summary: A weak jobs report made an October hike less likely, so the Bank of Canada is waiting on today's inflation numbers. A hot reading would put a hike back on the table and help the loonie.

banks.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand

sources.label: ActionForex: NZ trade deficit NZ$1.97B, fuel +96%
Finimize (Oct 16): ANZ sees NZ inflation cooling (3.8% vs 4.1%)
FXStreet/BBH (Oct 20): RBNZ Oct-28 hike odds ~80%

banks.detail: Oct 28 hike odds firmed to 80-85% (BBH/FXStreet swaps; BNZ/Westpac/ASB research) — up from the two-way call. BNZ PMI 56.5 (strongest since 2021, 15th straight expansion) feeds the hike side; NZ trade miss (NZ$1.97B vs 0.78B fc) feeds the hold side. Conway: direction 'most likely up'. NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT is the decider (ANZ 3.8% y/y vs 4.1% Q2; RBNZ proj 3.9%).
banks.summary: The RBNZ is split between hiking and holding on October 28. Business activity is strong but trade and food prices are soft, so Wednesday's inflation figure will decide it.

banks.name: European Central Bank

sources.label: Reuters (Oct 8): ECB to hold Oct 29, hike again in December (poll)
Reuters (Oct 19): Dollar firmer, euro weakens as French protests turn violent
UBS via Investing.com (Oct 20): ECB Oct move priced 2-3bp; Dec hike to 2.75%

banks.detail: October 29 is NOT priced as a hike — UBS (Oct 20): October move priced at 2-3bp; OIS 98.2% hold. December is the live meeting (Reuters poll: 64/73 expect +25bp to 2.75%). September CPI confirmed at 3.8% (three-year high, energy +18.9%). New: violent French protests pushed the OAT-Bund spread to ~147bp Monday (+9.9bp) — the euro's first real negative driver in days; EUR/USD 1.1229.
banks.summary: The ECB is expected to hold in October and is leaning toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

banks.name: Bank of Japan

sources.label: Reuters relay (Oct 18): BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation 'quite close' to 2% target
FXStreet (Oct 6): The market is pricing a BoJ pause — Oct-30 hike ~25%
Polymarket (Oct 17): BoJ Oct hold 96.5%

banks.detail: Ueda's clearest hawkish phrase yet: underlying inflation 'quite close' to the 2% target — firms December (Bloomberg/FXStreet: swaps ~88% Dec; TONA OIS ~64.5%) while Oct 29-30 stays a hold (~93-96%; Polymarket). Officials lean against back-to-back hikes after Sep 18. The ~216bp US-Japan 10Y gap is the weight; USD/JPY 158.50. Japan national CPI Fri is the last data before the meeting (fresh quarterly forecasts).
banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December rather than October. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen.

banks.name: Reserve Bank of Australia

sources.label: Reuters via Jack FM (Oct 19): Kent — unsure policy is 'restrictive enough'
RBA: Fireside Chat at the CBA Global Markets Conference (transcript, Oct 19)

banks.detail: Kent (CBA fireside chat): 'reasonable evidence' neutral rates are rising — unsure 4.60% is 'restrictive enough'; called the post-jobs trimming of hike odds 'sensible'. Nov 2-3 hike ~30%, December ~50%. Underlying inflation 3.6% for three straight months; labor loosening 'faster than forecast' (4.7% unemp, 5-yr high). Q3 CPI Oct 28 is the pivot. Monday: Kent added the labour market is loosening 'faster than expected' — a dovish lean inside the hawkish setup. China GDP 4.5% beat the demand read; AUD/USD ~0.6981, the day's best G10 performer.
banks.summary: The RBA's tone has turned more hawkish, hinting rates may not be high enough yet. A hike in November is possible but not expected, and next week's inflation number is the key test.

banks.name: Bank of England
banks.priced: November 5: hike ~95% (to 4.00%); December the open question.

sources.label: FXStreet (Oct 19): UK data-packed week — Deutsche Bank CPI preview (3.49%)
CMC Markets: The week ahead — UK CPI, Meta and Tesla earnings

banks.detail: Nov 5 hike ~95% priced; the question is December. UK CPI consensus hardened to 3.4% y/y (prev 3.1%; Deutsche 3.49%) — prints Wed 1am CT. UK labor Tue 1am CT (unemp 5.0% fc vs 4.9%; earnings 3.8% vs 3.9%). Bailey speaks Wednesday; Oct 28 budget. GBP/USD 1.3313 (Tue ~1:25am CT).
banks.summary: The Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5, and the debate is already about December. This week's UK jobs and inflation data will shape how far it goes.

banks.name: Swiss National Bank
banks.priced: Holding at 0%; a December cut is possible.

sources.label: Reuters (Oct 19): Dollar firmer, euro weakens (Asia FX read)

banks.detail: 0.00% held; December cut risk stays on the table with PPI soft (+0.3% vs 0.6%). No Swiss driver — the Beirut haven-bid tailwind never fired at Monday's open (no Hezbollah retaliation yet). USD/CHF 0.8254 (Tue ~1:25am CT). SNB meeting write-up Thursday.
banks.summary: The SNB is holding rates at zero and could even cut in December, because Swiss inflation is very low. The franc moves more on global fear than on Swiss news right now.
